Report DescriptionTHE CALLER IS REPORTING A SHORT OF FOUR 18650 CELL LITHIUM ION BATTERIES FROM AN ELECTRIC CIGARETTE IN THE THERMAL RUNAWAY WHILE AMERICAN AIRCRAFT 642 WAS STILL AT THE GATE. THE INCIDENT OCCURRED WHEN THE PASSENGER WAS SECURING THE CHARGER THAT CONTAINED 4 BATTERIES, IN THEIR CARRY-ON BAG UNDER THEIR SEAT, WHEN THEY MADE CONTACT WITH ANOTHER TYPE OF METAL CAUSING THE BATTERIES TO SHORT AND START A FIRE IN THE PASSENGER CARRY-ON BAG. TWO PASSENGERS SUSTAINED MINOR INJURIES, RECEIVED ON SITE FIRST AID BY FIRST RESPONDERS AND RELEASED. THE SMOKING BAG WAS REMOVED FROM THE AIRCRAFT AND PROPERLY MITIGATED BY AIRPORT FIRE FIGHTERS.

properties.title: NRC Report: Alkaline Water near Providence, RI
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 1474206 - Medium Affected: OTHER - Suspected Responsible Party: ELECTROLIZING INC
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1474206
Incident Time: 2026-07-31 08:00:00
Nearest City: Providence, RI
Location: 10 HOUGHTON ST
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: ALKALINE WATER
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party: ELECTROLIZING INC
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.8566, -71.43561 (Approximated from street_address)
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTING THE RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF CHROMIC ACID, FROM A PROCESSING TANK, TO A SECONDARY CONTAINMENT TANK DUE TO A TANK RUPTURE. IT IS BELIEVED THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT TANK MAY HAVE ALSO BEEN BREACHED AND IS RELEASING MATERIAL TO AREAS UNDERNEATH THE FACILITY. THE STEEL SUPPORT STRUCTURE OF THE TANK HAS BEEN EXPOSED TO CHROMIC ACID AND IS ACTIVELY CORRODING. ADDITIONALLY, CHROMIC ACID HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE LEAKING THROUGH CINDER BLOCK WALLS AND IS BELIEVED TO BE COMING FROM THE AIR SCRUBBING SYSTEM, THOUGH THE SOURCE COULD NOT BE CONFIRMED BY THE CALLER. EMPLOYEES HAVE BEEN INSTRUCTED TO CLEAN THE WALLS AND PAINT OVER THE CHROMIC ACID STAIN. CALLER STATED A BOILER SYSTEM HAS A WATER FED TANK THAT RECYCLES THE WATER IN THE STEAM SYSTEM AND HAS SHOWN 11 PH WHEN CONSISTENTLY TESTED. THE BOILER DISCHARGES EXTRA ALKALINE WATER INTO THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT WHEN APPROACHING FULL LEVELS. OTHER PROCESSING TANKS SHARE THE SAME IMPACTED CONTAINMENT TANK, SO THERE IS A MIXTURE OF ALKALINE WATER, CHROMIC ACID, AND VARIOUS OTHER MATERIALS IN THE RUPTURED CONTAINMENT TANK. IMPACT TO VEGETATION WAS NOTED BY THE CALLER. OSHA INSPECTIONS (31JUL2026) HAVE BEEN COMPLETED BUT INFORMATION REGARDING THE INSPECTIONS HAVE NOT BEEN PROVIDED TO CITY COUNCILMAN AND/OR EMPLOYEES. EMPLOYEES HAVE EXPERIENCED NEGATIVE HEALTH SYMPTOMS (I.E RESPIRATORY ISSUES). MEDICAL ATTENTION HAS BEEN SOUGHT CITING POTENTIAL CHEMICAL EXPOSURE.

Report Description
ON 4/23/2012 AT 7:30 A.M. DURING PRODUCTION, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE PURGE SOLVENT COLLECTION HEADER LOCATED INSIDE THE PAINT SYSTEM 1 PAINT PLANT (COLOR 2 BOOTH) HAD AN EQUIPMENT FAILURE. THIS RESULTED IN 185 GALLONS OF WASTE PURGE SOLVENT FLOWING INTO THE WASTE WATER RECIRCULATION SYSTEM USED TO RECOVER PAINT SOLIDS. WE HAVE CALCULATED THAT 185 GALLONS (1350.5 POUNDS AT 7.3 POUNDS/GALLON) OF WASTE PURGE SOLVENT WAS RELEASE INTO THE FLOOD SHEET WHICH RESULTED IN THE SOLVENT BEING EMITTED INTO THE AIR. THE WASTE PURGE SOLVENT IS A BLEND OF MANY SOLVENTS WHICH CARRIES THE HAZARDOUS WASTE CODE OF D001, F003, AND D035. THE MOST STRINGENT RQ THRESHOLD OF THESE WASTE CODES IS 100 POUNDS FOR THE F003 WASTE THEREFORE THIS SPILL EXCEEDED THE THRESHOLD FOR REPORTING.

Report Description
********WEB REPORT********* HYDRAULIC LINE ON "TRASH RACK" AT THE RIVER MILL DAM BROKE AND RELEASED APPROXIMATELY ONE GALLON OF FOOD GRADE HYDRAULIC FLUID. A "TRASH RACK" IS THE PIECE OF EQUIPMENT THAT REMOVES DEBRIS FROM THE WATER UPSTREAM OF THE POWER GENERATING TURBINES IN THE RIVER MILL DAM. THE HYDRAULIC LINE WAS ISOLATED AND THE RELEASE OF MATERIAL WAS STOPPED. THE SPILL OCCURRED DIRECTLY UPSTREAM OF TURBINE #5 SO IT PASSED THROUGH THE TURBINE AND DOWNSTREAM IMMEDIATELY. MAINTENANCE CREW USED ABSORBENT MATERIALS TO CLEANUP OIL SPILLED ON THE DECK AND SLIGHT SHEEN OBSERVED IN EDDY DOWNSTREAM OF THE DAM.

properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 947457 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: EXTERRAN
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 947457
Incident Time: 2010-07-12 13:30:00
Nearest City: Gobernador, NM
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: WASTE OIL/LUBRICANTS - POSS. CON
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: EXTERRAN
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 35 gallons
TUBING LINE BROKE ON A HOT START FOR A LARGE COMPRESSOR ENGINE. THE HOT START RECIRCULATES OIL TO KEEP IT WARM WHEN THE ENGINE ISN'T OPERATING, TO ALLOW THE ENGINE TO BE SAFELY STARTED IN COLD CONDITIONS. THE HOT START IS SITUATED IN A CONCRETE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AT GROUND LEVEL, WHICH HAS DRAIN LINES TO A BULK TANK TO STORE THE RELEASED OIL IF NEEDED. UNKNOWN TO THE EQUIPMENT OPERATOR, THE DRAIN LINES WERE PLUGGED AND DID NOT ALLOW THE RELEASED OIL TO PROPERLY FLOW TO THE BULK TANK. DUE TO THIS, APPROX. 25 TO 35 GALLONS OF USED OIL WAS RELEASED TO THE SURROUNDING SOIL.

USED COOKING OIL IS BURNED TO CREATE A HEATING FUEL FOR THE HOME AT THIS RESIDENCE. ON TUESDAY, 6/8, TRASH WAS BURNED IN A BURN BARREL NEAR A BUILDING. THERE IS A POND OF OIL ON THE GROUND NEAR THIS BURN BARREL THAT CAUGHT FIRE AND SPREAD TO THE BUILDING AND DESTROYED A WAGON. SEVERAL FIRE DEPARTMENTS WERE THERE TO PUT THE FIRE OUT. THERE IS A VERY STRONG OIL ODOR ON THE PROPERTY. THE WATER USED TO PUT THE FIRE OUT CAUSED THE OIL TO SPREAD TO AN AREA WHERE THE HOMEOWNER'S DOG WAS ABLE TO DRINK IT CAUSING HIM TO BECOME SICK (THROWING UP). BABY GOATS IN THE NEARBY BARN GOT LOOSE AND GOT INTO THE AREA - THEY ARE NOW OIL COVERED.

Report Description
CALLER STATED THAT ON JULY 29TH 2013, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:30 AM, EXXON MOBILE CONFIRMED THAT TWO LINES WITHIN THE REFINERIES FLARE SYSTEM WERE ACTUALLY OPEN ON BOTH ENDS OF EACH LINE. AS A RESULT, NOT ALL VENT GAS FLOW THAT MIGHT HAVE GONE TO THE TWO EMERGENCY UPRIGHT FLARES DURING PRIOR FLARING EVENTS WERE MEASURED. AT 1:30 PM THE SAME DAY THE LINES WERE CLOSED OFF. AFTER SUBSEQUENT ANALYSIS, JUST COMPLETED THE REFINERY BELIEVES THAT WE EXCEEDED THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF 1000 POUNDS FOR NITROGEN MONOXIDE (NO) DURING EIGHT FLARING EVENTS OVER THE PAST FIVE YEARS THAT WERE NOT PREVIOUSLY REPORTED. THE REFINERY CONTINUES TO OPERATE. THESE PAST EVENTS HAVE HAD NO IMPACT ON PRODUCTION.
